name: Inside Out
label: Revelation
lede: One seven-inch, fewer than three years, a final show in Long Beach, and a song title from the record they never made that ended up on the side of a band that filled stadiums.

eras.title: The side project that stopped being one
eras.text: Inside Out started as a sideline for two guitarists in the Orange County band Hard Stance. It took a drummer's push and a new guitar player to turn it into the band Zack de la Rocha actually sang in, pulling from Minor Threat, Bad Brains, Dag Nasty and, as the songs got heavier, Led Zeppelin.

years.h: Two [[Hard Stance|3029fc29-bf7c-4f78-8bfc-97c0bf144c6d]] guitarists try something on the side
years.p: [[Zack de la Rocha|aa659468-db56-41c9-b6fe-61f4bb2ef1a6]] and Rob Haworth both play guitar in Hard Stance. Inside Out is their extra band, with de la Rocha out front on vocals.

q: There was something really sincere in his eyes when he was singing.
years.h: Inside Out's first show, and Alex Barreto's push
years.p: Inside Out start at the bottom of a bill in the fall. Alex Barreto, Hard Stance's drummer, joins and is the one who talks Zack de la Rocha into taking the band seriously.
years.xp: Barreto saw the singer before most people did. De la Rocha had been a guitarist in Hard Stance, and Inside Out was the first band where he stood at the mic.

years.p: Vic DiCara, fresh from New York's Beyond, replaces Rob Haworth and Inside Out's sound opens up. As DiCara put it later, they took a little of everything they liked instead of copying one subgenre.

years.h: Mark Haworth and Chris Bratton join Inside Out
years.p: Mark Haworth, Rob Haworth's brother and another Hard Stance alum, takes bass. [[Chris Bratton|cbaf85ca-1bc7-4eb0-b9cb-ca5d8773b27f]], of [[No for an Answer|23d26104-95e2-473f-a704-ab0bcd702da3]] and [[Chain of Strength|81a3c11e-ac20-4bb4-8614-06b157e802d8]], replaces Alex Barreto on drums before the sessions.

eras.title: Four songs Revelation can't keep in the racks
eras.text: One record, one East Coast trip, one radio session. That's the whole official output, and it's been enough for Revelation to call it possibly the most popular release the label has ever put out.

years.h: Inside Out tour east with [[Shelter|d5157104-76b1-4b8b-90c2-9ff994f940db]] and [[Quicksand|3c9f8bef-a658-4204-9ee8-7e95d2535b32]]
years.p: Inside Out's one East Coast run, a June package with Ray Cappo's Shelter and the new Quicksand. The van's engine seized on day one and Revelation's Jordan Cooper paid to fix it.
years.xp:
On June 28 they played the Unisound in Reading, PA; a VHS of that set surfaced 26 years later.

The tour ran out of New York through Buffalo, Cleveland and City Gardens in New Jersey. A VHS of the Reading set surfaced 26 years later.

The roadie crew included former Beyond singer Kevin Egan and a young [[Derrick Green|eb624b5f-6580-42d4-af83-19fad8e866ab]], years before he fronted [[Sepultura|1d93c839-22e7-4f76-ad84-d27039efc048]]. Egan later wrote the tour up for No Echo, clean-sock shortage and all.

years.p: Four songs on the original seven-inch, six on the later CD. Revelation calls it possibly its most popular release ever, and praises Zack de la Rocha's vocal as intense as anything on a hardcore record.
years.xp:
Twenty years later an Orange County record store manager told OC Weekly it still sold once or twice a week, and they never let it go out of stock.

The record kept doing its work on bands that came later: Wikipedia lists [[Refused|42884e27-dfb8-453d-990f-2ffd90bc2d1a]], [[Have Heart|e519e012-e1a3-4592-b3f6-5a16227ab654]], [[Turnstile|7b748dac-f5ce-45a7-9b95-c1d8b5b013ed]] and even [[Linkin Park|f59c5520-5f46-4d2c-b2c4-822eabf53419]] among those who drew from it.

years.p: A session on KXLU, the Loyola Marymount college station, captures Inside Out's unreleased songs at broadcast quality, the best-sounding record of the material that came after No Spiritual Surrender.

years.h: "No Spiritual Surrender" live at the Anthrax, Norwalk CT, June 1990
yt: "No Spiritual Surrender" live at the Anthrax, Norwalk CT, June 1990

eras.title: A monk, a last show, and a band name
eras.text: Vic DiCara's turn to Krishna consciousness ended the band. What was left behind was a finished set of new songs, including one called Rage Against the Machine, a title that would be famous by the end of the next year.

years.h: Vic DiCara leaves Inside Out for the Krishna temple
years.p: Shortly after No Spiritual Surrender, Vic DiCara joins [[Ray Cappo|e8357f9d-f7f5-4858-a766-aef004bb38a6]]'s Krishna-conscious [[Shelter|d5157104-76b1-4b8b-90c2-9ff994f940db]], becomes a Hare Krishna monk, and later starts [[108|7f0c252a-bd45-4fe0-b306-478eeb07b97b]].

years.h: Inside Out's last show: Long Beach
years.p: The final set includes songs meant for a second record, among them Darkness of Greed and one called Rage Against the Machine. A clean remaster of the tape turns up in 2013.

years.big: Inside Out's next record was going to be called Rage Against the Machine
years.h: Zack de la Rocha takes Inside Out's second-album title with him
years.p: Inside Out is done by the fall. Zack de la Rocha takes the unused title to Los Angeles, where he, [[Tom Morello|42a636a0-dbe4-4d0c-abe2-1590fad9531b]], [[Tim Commerford|4d61abe3-ce6d-4383-b2cd-8b4491496549]] and [[Brad Wilk|b48aebac-8c3e-48aa-b5e6-2b38f30f5f78]] become [[Rage Against the Machine|3798b104-01cb-484c-a3b0-56adc6399b80]].
years.xp:
The planned follow-up to No Spiritual Surrender had a working title, Rage Against the Machine, and a song to match. Neither came out under the Inside Out name.

Within a year it was the name of a band signed to Epic.

Mark Haworth went on to State of the Nation, Alex Barreto to Statue.

eras.title: The tape-trader's band
eras.text: With one official record, Inside Out's afterlife has run on bootlegs, surfacing tapes and younger bands. Every few years another piece of the story shows up.

years.p: Oktopus of [[Dälek|4f2c4842-f90f-476e-95d3-8e868ae4d745]] turns Inside Out's No Spiritual Surrender into Ghost in the Machine for the mashup album Threat: Music That Inspired the Movie.

years.h: No Spiritual Surrender, still a weekly seller
years.p: OC Weekly checks in twenty years on: Inside Out's EP moves once or twice a week at a local Orange County shop, and the store reorders whenever it runs out.

years.h: Inside Out's last show, finally in good sound
years.p: A high-quality remaster of the May 18, 1991 Long Beach set surfaces, with the never-released Rage Against the Machine and Darkness of Greed.

years.h: VHS of Inside Out's Reading show turns up
years.p: Footage of the June 28, 1990 show at the Unisound in Reading, Pennsylvania, appears online.
Bandcamp Daily marks the anniversary with Tony Rettman's oral history. Alex Barreto's summary: Inside Out had something special, rehearsing or on stage.

years.h: Inside Out's Instagram asks which line-up for 2024
years.p: Inside Out's Instagram posts Sacrifice with the caption "For 2024 which line up?" and news sites run with it. The line-up question was never publicly answered.

For the Live Lounge, the Baltimore band covers Inside Out's Burning Fight, with singer Brendan Yates channeling Zack de la Rocha. A thirty-five-year-old song from a band with one EP, on national radio in Britain.
